question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}84 & ≡16\cdot 5+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡16\cdot 0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 102 & ≡20\cdot 5+2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡20\cdot 0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}84\cdot 102 & ≡4\cdot 2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡8\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡5+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
84\cdot 102\text{ mod }5=3.
$$
